title: Current, number density and drift speed
prior_knowledge_summary: AS Topic 1 quantities and units, including SI base units, derived units and unit conversions.
learning_goals: Use I = Anvq for a current-carrying conductor.
Relate microscopic carrier motion to macroscopic current.
new_learning: Number density, cross-sectional area and mean drift speed in the current equation.
not_yet_taught: define the potential difference across a component as the energy transferred per unit charge
recall and use V = W / Q
recall and use P = VI, P = I 2R and P = V 2 / R
sketch the I–V characteristics of a metallic conductor at constant temperature, a semiconductor diode and a filament lamp
explain that the resistance of a filament lamp increases as current increases because its temperature increases
recall and use R = ρL / A
understand that the resistance of a light-dependent resistor (LDR) decreases as the light intensity increases
understand that the resistance of a thermistor decreases as the temperature increases (it will be assumed that thermistors have a negative temperature coefficient)
knowledge_boundary: Includes I = Anvq and unit-safe rearrangement. Potential difference and circuit-network methods are deferred.

can_assume: use, for a current-carrying conductor, the expression I = Anvq, where n is the number density of charge carriers

past_paper_evidence.whole_question_context_policy: Resolve through the topic P2 index and retain complete question context.
